title: Compound Assignment: +=
concept: x += 1 is shorthand for x = x + 1 — it adds a value to a variable and stores the result back.
why: Compound assignment operators reduce repetition, prevent typos, and make the intent clearer.
syntax_ref: variable += amount;  // Same as: variable = variable + amount
tips: `x += y` is exactly the same as `x = x + y` — just shorter
Use in loops for accumulation: `sum += value;`
common_mistakes: Writing `=+` instead of `+=` — `x =+ 5` assigns +5 (still 5), not x+5!
Using += with `let` — compiler will reject it
Thinking += is for Int only — it works with Float64 too: `price += 0.50`
